subject: en
source: English National Curriculum — English programmes of study: key stage 2 (Year 5), writing composition and English Appendix 2 (vocabulary, grammar and punctuation), DfE 2013

weeks.topic: Narrative: story openings that hook the reader
objectives: Identify how authors open stories in different ways
Write an opening that establishes setting and character
Use a range of sentence openers

weeks.topic: Expanded noun phrases and figurative language in settings
objectives: Use expanded noun phrases to convey complicated information concisely
Use similes and metaphors to describe settings
Choose vocabulary for effect

weeks.topic: Relative clauses
objectives: Use relative clauses beginning with who, which, where, when, whose and that
Identify the relative pronoun in a sentence
Punctuate embedded relative clauses with commas

weeks.topic: Myths and legends: planning a quest story
objectives: Identify the features of myths and legends
Plan a narrative with a hero, a quest and a challenge
Organise the plot into paragraphs

weeks.topic: Dialogue to convey character and advance action
objectives: Punctuate direct speech accurately
Use dialogue to show what characters are like
Vary reporting verbs and adverbs

weeks.topic: Parenthesis: brackets, dashes and commas
objectives: Use brackets, dashes or commas to indicate parenthesis
Add extra information without changing the main sentence
Choose the right punctuation for the tone

weeks.topic: Non-chronological reports: organising information
objectives: Use headings, subheadings and paragraphs to organise a report
Write in the present tense with formal, impersonal language
Include technical vocabulary

weeks.topic: Linking paragraphs with adverbials of time, place and number
objectives: Use adverbials of time, place and number to link ideas across paragraphs
Build cohesion within paragraphs using then, after that, this, firstly
Sequence a text logically

weeks.topic: Modal verbs and adverbs of possibility
objectives: Use modal verbs to show degrees of possibility
Use adverbs such as perhaps and surely
Choose modals to sound more or less certain

weeks.topic: Persuasive writing: letters and adverts
objectives: Identify persuasive techniques in letters and adverts
Use rhetorical questions, emotive language and the rule of three
Write a persuasive letter to a real audience

weeks.topic: Word building: verb prefixes and suffixes -ate, -ise, -ify
objectives: Convert nouns or adjectives into verbs using -ate, -ise and -ify
Use verb prefixes dis-, de-, mis-, over- and re-
Explain how prefixes change meaning

weeks.topic: Poetry: narrative poems (The Highwayman)
objectives: Explore how narrative poems tell a story
Identify rhythm, rhyme and repetition
Perform and write a narrative verse

weeks.topic: Newspaper reports
objectives: Identify the features of a newspaper report
Write a headline, lead paragraph and quotes
Use reported speech and the past tense

weeks.topic: Editing and proof-reading drafts
objectives: Evaluate and edit by assessing the effectiveness of own and others' writing
Propose changes to vocabulary, grammar and punctuation
Proof-read for spelling and punctuation errors

weeks.topic: Term 1 review: relative clauses, parenthesis and cohesion
objectives: Revisit Year 5 grammar from Term 1
Apply grammar in a short piece of writing
Use correct terminology

weeks.topic: Commas to clarify meaning and avoid ambiguity
objectives: Use commas to clarify meaning or avoid ambiguity
Use commas after fronted adverbials and in lists
Explain how a comma changes meaning

weeks.topic: Biography: writing a life story
objectives: Identify the features of a biography
Write in chronological order in the third person and past tense
Use time adverbials to link events

weeks.topic: Explanation texts: how and why things happen
objectives: Explain a process using cause and effect language
Use diagrams and captions to support writing
Write in the present tense with technical vocabulary

weeks.topic: Cohesion within paragraphs: pronouns and determiners
objectives: Use pronouns and determiners to avoid repetition
Check that pronoun references are clear
Build cohesive paragraphs around one main idea

weeks.topic: Playscripts: turning narrative into script
objectives: Identify the conventions of a playscript
Write stage directions and character lines
Convert a story scene into a playscript

weeks.topic: Narrative: building suspense and tension
objectives: Use short sentences and pacing to build tension
Use the senses to create atmosphere
Plan a cliffhanger ending

weeks.topic: Diary writing from a character's viewpoint
objectives: Write in the first person showing thoughts and feelings
Use informal language and a personal tone
Recount events in time order

weeks.topic: Precise vocabulary: synonyms, antonyms and the thesaurus
objectives: Use a thesaurus to choose precise vocabulary
Explore synonyms and antonyms with shades of meaning
Avoid repetition in writing

weeks.topic: Poetry: imagery, personification and metaphor
objectives: Identify imagery in poems
Use personification and metaphor to create pictures
Write a descriptive poem

weeks.topic: Discussion texts: presenting two viewpoints
objectives: Present arguments for and against an issue
Use connectives such as however and on the other hand
Write a balanced conclusion

weeks.topic: Consistent verb tenses: progressive and perfect forms
objectives: Use the progressive and perfect forms of verbs
Keep tenses consistent across a text
Mark relationships of time and cause with the perfect form

weeks.topic: Mid-year assessment: writing and grammar
objectives: Write an independent narrative or non-fiction piece
Complete a grammar and punctuation test
Apply Year 5 terminology

weeks.topic: Fables and folk tales from other cultures
objectives: Read and retell fables and folk tales from different cultures
Identify the moral or message
Write a modern version of a traditional tale

weeks.topic: Flashbacks and shifts in time in narrative
objectives: Identify flashbacks in stories
Use tense changes and adverbials to signal shifts in time
Write a story that includes a flashback

weeks.topic: Persuasive speech: rhetoric and delivery
objectives: Write a persuasive speech using rhetorical devices
Use emphasis and pauses when speaking
Respond to counter-arguments

weeks.topic: Leaflets and information brochures
objectives: Plan a leaflet for a specific audience
Use layout devices such as headings, bullet points and boxes
Write concise, informative text

weeks.topic: Poetry: free verse and shape poems
objectives: Explore poems without regular rhyme
Arrange words visually for effect
Write and present a free verse or shape poem

weeks.topic: Summary writing: identifying key points
objectives: Identify the main ideas in a text
Write a concise summary in own words
Remove unnecessary detail

weeks.topic: Extended narrative: plan, draft and publish
objectives: Plan a longer story with clear paragraphs
Draft and redraft using feedback
Publish a final version for an audience

weeks.topic: Grammar consolidation: Year 5 terminology
objectives: Use Year 5 terminology: modal verb, relative pronoun, relative clause, parenthesis, cohesion, ambiguity
Identify these features in texts
Apply them in own writing

weeks.topic: End-of-year assessment: Year 5 writing and grammar
objectives: Write an independent piece showing Year 5 features
Complete a grammar, punctuation and spelling test
Review own targets

weeks.topic: Year 5 review and readiness for Year 6
objectives: Reflect on progress in writing
Revisit key grammar and punctuation
Set writing targets for Year 6
